scope: One manually driven, open-ended helical tube screw from the family on 6r. The other pumps on the sheet are catalogue context, not merged into one invented machine.
gaps: The sheet carries no writing and does not establish a tube diameter, pitch, flow rate, material or efficiency.
The exact human-drive connections in the sheet are not dimensioned. Here the hand crank acts directly on the shaft.
Other water-raising mechanisms on6r and the unworkable recirculating arrangement1068v require separate geometry before display.

date.note: Approximate contextual date, not a dated inscription.

scale_m.note: Conservative swept envelope x +/-0.7 m, y 0 to 2.15 m, z -1.6 to 2 m. The hand crank sweeps above the tube. Numerical sampling of every part over 144 poses found max y 2.14256 m.

assumptions.statement: All numerical procedural dimensions, positions, angles and chosen material classes in parts and joints are modern modelling assumptions. They do not measure Leonardo’s sheet or any museum replica.
assumptions.reason: The sheet does not dimension a complete assembly.

joints.notes: Joint values add to the listed rest orientation. Positions are pivot-local for moving roots. Fixed children inherit motion.

drive.justification: Direct hand crank on joint turn. Rate selected to show the helix calmly. It is not a historical measured rate.

motion.visitor_12s: The crank and helical tube turn once. t is local seconds and pi=3.141592653589793. Accumulate angle after each loop. Flow is not represented by scripted rising particles.

animation_notes: Do not animate a mechanism missing from the evidence.
The open-ended tube rotates as a rigid assembly around its own axis. Water is not rigidly attached to it.
No perpetual recirculation. Human work is supplied at the crank.
No assumed volumetric output is shown in motion. Numerical output below is an explicitly assumed bucket-volume example.
Tube material leather and timber supports are C assumptions. The shaft axis rises30 degrees above horizontal.

sources.title: Vitruvius: On Architecture 10.6
sources.supports: Ancient water screw predates Leonardo. Its construction as the period knew it: a rounded beam as the shaft, its ends strengthened with iron nails and hoops and fitted with iron pivots, the pivots turning in iron-fitted cross pieces on beams right and left of the screw (10.6.3).
sources.limitations: Read in the Gwilt translation. The enclosed screw of planks is not built here; its shaft, hoops, pivots and frame are the type the tube screw is built to.

research.identification: [folio] CA6r, Ambrosiana. The digital edition marks the sheet as without writing.
sheet_vs_reconstruction: [sheet-description] Helical water-raising tubes occur among different pumps on the sheet.

[geometry] This original procedural screw selects a2.4 m helical tube axis, six turns and direct manual drive. It does not reproduce a museum model. [galileo]1068v is a separate attempted self-powered system.

[folio] The sheet draws the tube wound close round a thick round core. [ancient] The core, its hooped ends with iron pivots, and the frame of posts and cross pieces with iron-lined holes follow the construction Vitruvius 10.6.3 describes. [geometry] The bands, the pitch, the joinery, the troughs and the base are the museum's reconstruction of the type.

dimensions.note: No dimensional wording or Richter number has been verified. No historical braccio conversion is asserted.

claims.tested_by_leonardo: No direct test record established in the inspected sources.
claims.built_in_lifetime: No construction of this particular design in Leonardo’s lifetime is established. [ancient] The water screw was known in antiquity.
later_tests: No controlled performance test for this chosen6r geometry was found.

inputs.note: Assumed water volume delivered per screw revolution. This independent flow assumption is not calculated from the tube geometry.
Modern model screw rotation rate in revolutions per second, equal to the direct crank rate.
Assumed density of the water being raised.
Modern model vertical delivery height between intake and outlet.
Assumed efficiency from crank input power to gravitational potential energy gained by the water.
Modern model crank and screw angular speed, equal to 2*pi*n.

physics.result: Q=0.00004167 m^3/s=2.5 L/min. P_water=0.4905 W. At assumed eta0.35, P_in=1.40 W and torque2.68 N m. Volume per revolution is an independent illustrative assumption, not derived from the tube.
physics.limitations: This arithmetic is a conditional illustration, not an experimental result.
physics.verdict_en: An assumed delivery of 2.5 litres per minute through 1.2 metres needs about 1.4 watts at 35 percent efficiency.
physics.verdict_de: Angenommene 2,5 Liter pro Minute über 1,2 Meter Höhe brauchen bei 35 Prozent Wirkungsgrad etwa 1,4 Watt.

myths.claim: Leonardo invented the Archimedean screw or made it power itself.
myths.correction: [ancient] The screw predates him. [galileo]1068v records an attempted self-powered layout. With pump and wheel efficiencies below1, it cannot sustain circulation.

research.confidence: High for folio family, low for historical size and operating performance. Complete at stated modern screw scope.
